newsitem.title: USA: Conservative group seeks campaign finance probe.
newsitem.headline: Conservative group seeks campaign finance probe.

text.p: A conservative legal group Tuesday asked Attorney General Janet Reno for an independent investigation into whether Vice President Al Gore took part in unlawful campaign fundraising activities at a Buddhist temple.

The Landmark Legal Foundation said in a letter to Reno that the appointment of an independent counsel was warranted to investigate the fundraising at a Buddhist temple near Los Angeles as part of an April event attended by Gore.
"There is credible evidence that fundraising activities occurred at the tax-exempt Buddhist temple, where he was the featured guest, which is unlawful," wrote Mark Levin, the group's president.
"And there is credible evidence that at least one $5,000 campaign contribution was laundered through a Buddhist clergyman, which is also unlawful," he added.

Reno rejected Friday a request from five congressional Republicans for an independent probe into eight allegations on Democratic campaign fundraising from foreign sources, including the incident at the Buddhist temple.

It marked the third time Reno rejected a request for an independent counsel probe into campaign finance allegations. The Justice Department said all three requests failed to meet the law's requirement of "specific, credible evidence" that a person covered by the law had committed a federal crime.
